items.title: The yield on Japanese 10-year government bonds hit 3% today, for the first time in 30 years. I forecast this on my podcast when the BOJ drew a line in the sand at 50 basis points. This is a huge problem for Japan, but a harbinger of an even bigger problem for the U.S. Got Gold?

items.title: The higher the 10-year Treasury yield rises in anticipation of rate hikes, the less likely the Fed will hike. Even if it does hike 25 basis points, it'll be too little to reduce inflation. Plus, higher rates increase future budget deficits, raising both bond yields and inflation.

items.title: The yield on the 10-year Treasury is now 4.78%, the highest since 2007. The high from 2006 was 5.15%. Once that's taken out, the next target is the 1999 high of 6.44%, then the 1994 high of 8.03%. In 1994 the national debt was well under $5 trillion. Now it's over $40 trillion!

items.title: The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.75%, the highest since Jan. 2025. When the yield rises above 4.77%, it will be the highest since 2007. However, in 2007 Treasuries were still in a bull market, with yields headed lower. Now they're in a bear market, with yields headed much higher.

items.title: I bought a replacement part for my hyperbaric oxygen chamber for $283. FedEx billed me separately $28.30 for the tariffs and $17.50 to process the tariff payment. So in total, Trump's tariffs forced me to pay an extra 16.2% to import the item. The foreign producer paid nothing.
